MARCOS: GOV'T FULLY MOBILIZED TO RESPOND TO WIDESPREAD FLOODING

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday (Tuesday in Manila) assured the public that the national government is fully mobilized to address the widespread flooding caused by the enhanced southwest monsoon.

In a recorded message from Washington, D.C., where he is on a three-day official visit, President Marcos said he had directed all relevant agencies before leaving Manila to prepare for the severe weather and ensure the safety of affected communities.

He said the Office of Civil Defense, Department of Transportation, Department of Health, Department of Science and Technology, Department of Social Welfare and Development, Department of Public Works and Highways, Department of Energy, and the Department of the Interior and Local Government had been instructed to coordinate and deliver timely assistance.

Relief goods and medical teams have been deployed, while efforts to secure transportation, water, and electricity supplies in flooded areas are underway.

President Marcos also urged the public to remain vigilant and to follow advisories from local and national authorities.

He emphasized the need to further strengthen the government's disaster response capabilities in the face of intensifying climate change impacts.

Marcos is in the U.S. capital from July 20 to 22 for an official visit upon the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump.

PET RELIEF MISSION

Volunteers from the Philippine Animal Welfare Society (PAWS) braved the rains over the weekend as they delivered aid for pets affected by Tropical Storm Crising and the enhanced southwest monsoon.

About 200 relief packs were distributed Sunday across three communities in Quezon City to help families care for their cats and dogs amid ongoing flooding and evacuation.

PAWS said all goods came from its shelter stock. More teams are being prepared to reach other affected areas. The group is calling for donations of pet food, canned goods and rice, which may be dropped off daily from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. at the PAWS Animal Rehabilitation Center in Loyola Heights, Quezon City.

📸 PAWS via Facebook

'NANANATILING BUKAS ANG SIMBAHAN PARA SA LAHAT'

The Santa Lucia Parish in Novaliches, Quezon City, continues to serve as a temporary shelter for evacuees affected by the southwest monsoon or habagat, after opening its doors on Monday, July 21.

"Ang Simbahan ng Santa Lucia ay patuloy na kakanlungin at tutulungan ang ating mga kapatid na apektado ng baha dahil sa bagyo," the church said in a Facebook post.

The parish has also suspended today's Holy Mass while the church is being used as an evacuation center.

📷: Santa Lucia Parish - Diocese of Novaliches via Facebook

data.raw_text:
Sa gitna ng malakas na pag-ulan ngayong araw ay nilinis ng mga tauhan ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority ang ilang mga drainage inlet sa iba't ibang lugar sa Metro Manila na apektado ng pagbaha.

Mula sa mga drainage at kanal ay inalis ang mga bara na nagdudulot ng pagbaha sa lansangan. Ilan sa mga lugar na nilinis ng mga tauhan ng ahensiya ang:

- Ortigas Westbound Sidewalk malapit sa EDSA
- Tiongquiao Brgy. BF Int'l CAA Las Pinas City
- Osmeña highway mula Magallanes hanggang Buendia NB, Makati City 

Kapag naaalis ang bara at basurang dala ng pag-ulan ay mas napabibilis ang paghupa ng baha.

Patuloy ang paalala ng MMDA sa responsableng pagtatapon at pamamahala ng basura para maiwasan ang perwisyong dulot nito.

#mmda #mmdaatyourservice
